clue.text: Jack has little brothers around entrance

indicators.note: turned around, the word that follows is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
bros is the shortened, little form of brothers

explanation.surface: A boy called Jack has his small brothers clustered about the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway noun, but it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable: to hold someone spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to hold their attention completely, which is what a gripping story does when it engrosses its reader.

clue.text: You can, by dancing about, show cheerfulness

indicators.note: letters that are dancing about move around and land in a fresh order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is told that a bit of dancing will prove they are in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyancy in the figurative sense is a light, resilient high spirits, the mood of someone who keeps bobbing back up.

clue.text: Upset about change

blocks.note: over means about or concerning, as in fussing over something
a turn is a change of direction or fortune

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a change in their circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the emotional state, but it is the verb meaning to knock over or reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a vase or a verdict is to upset it, tipping it over or reversing the decision.

clue.text: Stop person outside getting a look

indicators.note: the second word sits outside the first, wrapping around it on both sides

blocks.note: a being is a living creature, a person
to hold is to stop or delay, as in hold the train

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt somebody standing outside so you can take a look at them.
explanation.definitionFit: Beholding is an old-fashioned word for seeing or viewing, so someone beholding a thing is having a look at it.

clue.text: Extended sound range of river battle

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a fight or scrap

explanation.surface: It reads like a geography note on how far the noise of a river battle carried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound range' suggests acoustics over a landscape; it is a singing voice pushed above its natural register.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the technique by which a male singer pitches his voice above its normal register, stretching its compass upward.

clue.text: Saint listed oddly as March the first

indicators.note: letters set down in an odd way have been put out of their usual order

blocks.note: all four words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A saint whose feast is curiously recorded as falling on the first of March.
explanation.walkthrough: The first of March is in fact St David's Day, which makes the date look genuine; the saint meant is St Nicholas.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas grew out of Saint Nicholas, the bishop whose gift-giving legend became the figure also called Santa Claus.

clue.text: Contents of cake to do in a frying-pan

indicators.note: the contents are what sit inside the following word, so one piece goes within it

blocks.note: to cake is to harden or solidify, which is to set
to do someone in is to kill them

explanation.surface: Instructions for what to put into a cake mixture to cook it in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to harden, so its contents are what sits inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a heavy, long-handled pan used for frying, the American term for a frying-pan.

clue.text: Give Tom a drink - it shows approval

blocks.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale
a sup is a mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: Pour Tom something to drink and he will signal his satisfaction.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb's surname is the whole trick: give him a sup and the two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumbs-up is the familiar hand gesture of a raised thumb signalling that all is well or agreed.

clue.text: Triumph beneath worn flag

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath places the triumph word lower in the column, so it is written second

blocks.note: something worn is old and used
glory is the honour of a triumph

explanation.surface: A victory celebrated under a tattered banner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'beneath' means the triumph word is written below the worn one.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the traditional nickname of the United States national banner, the Stars and Stripes.

clue.text: To some extent that's not relevant outside Maine

indicators.note: the phrase sits outside, wrapped around the state abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: so what? is the dismissive reply meaning that does not matter
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: Someone half-concedes that a point about Maine is beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat means rather or to a moderate degree, a partial amount, which is what to some extent conveys.

clue.text: Two pounds easily convertible

blocks.note: L is the sign for a pound, and a second pound, a quid, is written as I QUID, one quid

explanation.surface: A sum of two pounds is the kind of money that is easy to change.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the pound sign from Latin libra; one quid, with I for one, makes the second pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid assets are those readily turned into cash, the financial sense of being easily convertible.

clue.text: Counterfeit money receiver put in prison

indicators.note: one thing put in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: base coin is debased or counterfeit money
a till is the drawer that receives money in a shop

explanation.surface: A man who handled fake money is sent to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counterfeit money receiver' reads as a fence for forged notes; split it, and base wraps around the till.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state jail, whose storming in 1789 began the French Revolution.

clue.text: See in our islands a pupil in comprehensive

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Great Britain, the islands of a British setter
lo! is an old exclamation meaning look or see
taken as written
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A look at Britain's islands, where a child is a pupil at a comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state school taking children of all abilities; here the word is the adjective meaning all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means covering the whole of something, all-inclusive and worldwide, which is what comprehensive also suggests.

clue.text: On a car, it could provide protection against the weather

indicators.note: could signals a possible version of the letters, one they might be rearranged into

blocks.note: the three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cover fitted on a car might shield it from rain and wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A raincoat is a waterproof outer garment worn to keep its wearer dry in wet conditions.

clue.text: I'm afraid we entered into a second exchange

definitions.note: a whole statement standing for an adjective: the speaker is struck with fear

indicators.note: a word that has entered into another now sits inside it

blocks.note: A as written, then S for second
taken as written
truck is an old word for barter or exchange, as in have no truck with

explanation.surface: An apologetic admission that we got into a quick argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm afraid' sounds like a polite apology, but it is the definition: a speaker who is overcome with dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with awe, a mix of wonder and fear, so it describes someone who is afraid.

clue.text: Layman, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the wordplay depends on how the word is spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: split after its third letter: lay is the definition, and man is a him, a pronoun pronounced the same as the sacred song

explanation.surface: It poses as a definition of an ordinary person with no professional training, judged on how the word sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layman' looks like one word for a non-expert; split it into lay, a song, and man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old poetic word for a song or ballad, and a hymn is a song of praise.

clue.text: On a trip, notes are read aloud, in the main

indicators.note: something read aloud is heard rather than seen, so the sound counts here

blocks.note: someone on a drug trip is high
the musical note C, in the plural, said out loud

explanation.surface: On a journey somebody reads musical notes out loud, chiefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like the everyday phrase for mostly; the main is the old poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary term for the open ocean, and the high seas are the open waters beyond any coastline.

clue.text: In time, I look up 'Menhir'

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the words are read from bottom to top
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a month is a period of time
I as written, and lo, an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone looks up an unfamiliar word in a dictionary in time.
explanation.walkthrough: A menhir is a standing stone, such as those in Brittany or Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A monolith is a single great block of stone set upright, exactly what a prehistoric menhir is.

clue.text: Active agent investing capital in Russia

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening letter, the one written large
to invest is to clothe or surround, so the agent wraps around the letter

blocks.note: a secret agent is a spy
the initial of Russia

explanation.surface: A busy secret agent puts money into Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing capital' reads as finance; investing means surrounding and capital means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, typically elderly, who is lively and nimble on their feet.

clue.text: Alas, one's unfortunately confined to certain times

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome has gone awry, so the letters come out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A sad remark that someone is, sadly, restricted to particular hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal things, like fruit or holiday work, occur only during particular parts of the year.

clue.text: Free ball affords relief

blocks.note: to rid is to free, as in rid the house of mice
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A dance with no ticket price is a welcome treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free ball' suggests a party with no entry charge; free is the verb to rid.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is being freed from something unwanted, as in good riddance, which brings a feeling of relief.

clue.text: Wrong time for George I to interrupt victory celebration

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another word

blocks.note: an age is a long period of time
GR, George Rex, is the royal cipher of a King George
taken as written
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: An awkward moment for the first King George to cut in on a victory party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to treat someone unjustly; the king breaks into the time word, not the celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to cause them distress by treating them unfairly, which is to do them wrong.

clue.text: Greeting, universally bad weather forecast

blocks.note: universally means for all
hail is a bad weather outlook, ice falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A weather presenter's greeting announces grim conditions everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forecast' slyly recalls Macbeth's witches, whose all-hail greetings foretold his future.
explanation.definitionFit: All hail is an archaic salutation of welcome or homage, a ceremonious way of saluting someone.

clue.text: Bear round Los Angeles is fair game

indicators.note: turned round, the word is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh, the famous bear
LA is the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A bear prowling around Los Angeles is fair game for hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' is the idiom for a legitimate target; read literally it is a game at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoop-la is a fairground stall where players toss rings over prizes, so it is literally a game at a fair.

clue.text: Reserve ready for the decider perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: to keep something back for later use
second meaning, read as three words: a team picked, or set, ahead of a deciding match

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three words, set a side, and it is what a selector does before a deciding game.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside is to keep it in reserve, putting it apart for a later purpose.

clue.text: The Spanish pilgrim from Mecca returned as a prophet

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: el is the Spanish for the
a haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A Spanish pilgrim who came back from Mecca was hailed as a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is the Old Testament prophet who was carried up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

clue.text: The time, they say, for grief

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the clue relies on the sound

blocks.note: the early part of the day, spoken

explanation.surface: People say there is a proper period set aside for grieving.
explanation.definitionFit: Mourning is the outward expression of sorrow for someone who has died, and so a state of grief.

clue.text: Northern town redeveloped, none the less one left

indicators.note: something left behind is dropped, so those letters are taken away
a redeveloped site is rebuilt in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the phrase taken letter for letter
the letters to drop from the phrase

explanation.surface: A northern town is rebuilt even so, with one resident remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helens is a town in Merseyside, near Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helens is an industrial town in the north-west of England, famous for glassmaking and rugby league.

clue.text: Good order for a Scots tailor?

blocks.note: first meaning: proper working condition
second meaning, whimsical: a maker of the Highland skirt

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: a tailor who makes kilts would be one, by analogy with hatter or potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilter means good condition or working order, now heard mostly in the phrase out of kilter.
